status_note: active (ghost 6.65.1-rc.0; Node 22/24); monorepo with ghost/core (Express app), admin (Ember + React apps), and many @tryghost/* packages.
core_problem: An opinionated, batteries-included publishing platform: posts/pages with a Lexical content model rendered to HTML, Handlebars themes driven by routes.yaml, members, paid tiers (Stripe), newsletters/email delivery, comments, ActivityPub, and a read-only Content API for headless use.
architecture: ghost/core/core/server is an Express monolith over Bookshelf/Knex (MySQL 8 in prod, SQLite dev) with a hand-maintained table schema (server/data/schema/schema.js: posts has mobiledoc, lexical, html, plaintext, status, visibility, type, custom_template, canonical_url, newsletter_id...). Content model: posts store Lexical JSON (`lexical` column); server/lib/lexical.js renders it to the cached `html` column via @tryghost/kg-lexical-html-renderer with DEFAULT_NODES from @tryghost/kg-default-nodes (cards: image, gallery, bookmark, html, callout, product, signup, email CTA...), with render options for image transforms and feature flags; `validate()` renders with a throwing error handler to reject malformed docs; server/lib/mobiledoc.js keeps the legacy Mobiledoc card factory and @tryghost/kg-converters migrates mobiledoc->lexical. API layer: server/api/endpoints/* framework-style descriptors (docName, browse/read/edit with option allow-lists, permissions, cache keys) — posts-public.js is the Content API for posts (options include/filter/fields/formats/limit/order/page; formats html|plaintext; read by id|slug|uuid) served under web/api/endpoints/content. Frontend: routes.yaml (default: collections `/` permalink `/{slug}/` template index; taxonomies tag/author) parsed by services/route-settings and turned by frontend/services/routing/router-manager.js into StaticRoutesRouter, CollectionRouter, TaxonomyRouter, StaticPagesRouter, PreviewRouter registered in a registry; rendering via frontend/services/rendering (renderer, templates, format-response) through the theme-engine (express-hbs instance, helpers under frontend/helpers, partials). Themes are Handlebars packages validated by gscan (server/services/themes/validate.js: gscan.check/checkZip against the Ghost major version; `canActivate = !results.hasFatalErrors`; warnings hidden in production). Members/newsletters/tiers/offers/stripe/email-service/email-analytics/link-tracking/comments/recommendations/activitypub are services under server/services; scheduling via post-scheduling + jobs-service; the url service maintains resource URLs for the routing layer.
core_innovation: A vertically integrated publisher: one content model (Lexical -> cached HTML) fanned out to web (routes.yaml + Handlebars), email newsletters, RSS and a Content API, with memberships and payments built in.
strengths: Lexical JSON as canonical content with pre-rendered `html`/`plaintext` columns: render once on write, serve static HTML — good for a near-zero-JS blog surface.

routes.yaml is a small declarative routing DSL (collections with permalink/filter/template, taxonomies, static routes with data bindings) compiled into router classes — a clean separation of URL structure from templates.
gscan theme validation with fatal-error gating before activation is a mature 'gate before ship' precedent for template packages, including version-targeted rule sets.
Content API is stable, cacheable, key-based read-only access with include/filter/fields/formats — trivially consumable by Astro at build time.
Complete newsletter/member stack (Stripe tiers, offers, email batching, analytics, link tracking, suppression lists) that would take years to rebuild; MIT.
weaknesses: Monolith: Express + Bookshelf + MySQL + its own admin (Ember/React) + Handlebars themes; not embeddable as a library, runs as a separate service per site or a Ghost(Pro) account.
Multi-tenancy absent: one Ghost instance = one site (Ghost(Pro) runs many instances); an agency would run N containers or pay per site.
Content model is post/page-centric with card-based rich text; no typed section/block schema, no design-system tokens, no fact provenance — irrelevant to SiteDefinition.
Themes are Handlebars, which would fight an Astro renderer; the visual identity of a client site would then be split across two template systems.
Very large codebase and release cadence (weekly minors) — operational burden for a blog add-on.
patterns_to_steal: Render-on-write: store canonical structured content and a pre-rendered html/plaintext alongside -> cache rendered section HTML fragments per SiteDefinition version for instant preview diffs and Lighthouse-stable output (renderer).

gscan-style versioned rule sets with fatal vs warning classes and `canActivate = !hasFatalErrors` -> the Launch QA gate and anti-slop tier 1 should be a versioned rule pack with fatal/warning severity and an explicit activation predicate (qa_gate / anti_slop).

routes.yaml declarative collections/taxonomies with permalink and filter -> page archetype to route mapping declared in the playbook (e.g. /services/{slug}/ bound to service facts) rather than hard-coded in the renderer (renderer / playbook).

Content API consumption pattern (key-based read-only, formats=html, filter/include) -> if a client needs a blog/newsletter, run Ghost as an external service and pull posts into Astro at build time via the Content API; keep it out of SiteDefinition (cms add-on).
patterns_to_avoid: Embedding Ghost into the agency runtime -> monolithic service, MySQL, own admin; only ever integrate over its Content API.
Handlebars themes for client sites -> conflicts with the Astro renderer and the design-system token model.
Card-based rich text (Lexical cards) as the page model -> free-form content with no fact binding or arrangement grammar.
reusable_patterns: RenderOnWriteCache: canonical structured content plus pre-rendered html/plaintext columns updated on save.
VersionedFatalWarningRulePack: validator rule sets keyed to a target version with fatal errors blocking activation and warnings advisory.
DeclarativeRouteMap: YAML collections/taxonomies/static routes with permalink and filter compiled into routers.
ReadOnlyContentAPI: key-scoped public read API with include/filter/fields/formats for static-site consumption.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for V1 and for the core architecture; it does not touch SiteDefinition, facts, design systems or the pipeline. Post-V1, if a client needs a blog or newsletter, the cheapest quality path is Ghost as an external managed service (Ghost(Pro) or a container) consumed by Astro at build time through the Content API, with the newsletter/member surface left entirely to Ghost — rather than rebuilding email delivery. Take two ideas now: gscan's fatal/warning versioned rule pack shape for our QA and anti-slop gates, and render-on-write caching of section HTML.
